Chapter 6: The Reading Life in a Busy World
Picture this: your day disappears in a whirlwind of meetings, errands, and never-ending to-dos. You finally get home, glance at the stack of unread books on your nightstand—and if you listen closely, you might almost hear them sigh.
Most of us don’t lack the desire to read—what we’re missing is the time and space to slip into a good story, especially with all the daily noise swirling around us. Remember how effortless it felt to lose yourself in books as a kid? These days, though, reading takes a bit more intention. You have to carve out those moments, and that’s not always easy.
Let me tell you about a parent I know. She’s juggling work and family life and often finds herself longing for those long, uninterrupted hours she once spent with a novel. Now, her reading happens in brief pockets—maybe ten minutes before bed, a couple of pages at lunch, a chapter while waiting in the carpool line.
At first, these tiny slivers of time felt frustrating, almost unsatisfying. But something interesting happened: she found a new rhythm. The stories she read became like old friends, their characters waiting patiently for her whenever she had a moment to return. Even a few stolen minutes turned into a little escape—a gentle reminder that her inner world was alive and well.
Others get creative too. Take the commuter who used to stare at endless traffic. Instead of losing that time, he started listening to audiobooks. Suddenly, those daily drives transformed from a boring routine into a private adventure—the car became his own personal theater.
Or think about the busy professional, swamped by a brand-new job, who decided to set a super modest goal: just one page a day. That’s it. Some days, it really was just a single page. Other times, one page turned into five, or ten. The key? The habit stayed alive.
Now, in our digital age, we face a whole new set of challenges—and opportunities. On one hand, e-readers and apps let us carry an entire library in our pockets. On the other, the constant buzz of notifications is always threatening to yank our attention away.
One reader, fed up with all the distractions, started turning off her phone every time she picked up a book. At first, it felt almost rebellious—like a radical act of reclaiming her focus in a world that expects us to always be available.
What becomes clear is that the reading life, just like any meaningful pursuit, needs some boundaries. Saying no to another episode, or scrolling through social media, usually means you’re saying yes to something better. For a lot of people, making time for books is a form of self-care—a way to feed both mind and spirit.
And you know what? The stories we read in these hard-won moments—they tend to stick with us. Maybe it’s because we had to fight a little for that space. Their impact lingers, and we walk away just a little richer for it.
